notes: C1 grammar as executable expectations. A relay's parser must map each input to the expected outcome. 'correction' means an immediate in-thread correction (never a modal) and NO domain event to the service. 'not_a_pull' means the message is ordinary channel traffic. The keyword is 'pull:' at message start, matched case-insensitively; the class word likewise, while the sentence is stored verbatim. Message-start-only is the one recognition rule the spec states (C1) and it stands. A message that opens with the keyword is an attempt: if it cannot be parsed it earns a correction, never silence. See ADR-0014 for why the earlier exact-token reading was dropped — the spec is silent on case, and a phone keyboard capitalises the first word of a message.

identical_event_rule.notes: C1: the optional /pull adapter and the canonical text grammar produce the IDENTICAL domain event, thread, and log entry. Usage is never compared by input method. A conforming relay must produce byte-equal domain events from both inputs across the full equality scope — matching only class and sentence does not conform.

equality.notes: Every field of the POSTed domain event (puller, class, sentence, origin tokens) must be equal between the two inputs; only the per-delivery identity (event_id) and timestamp may differ. The relay must also target the same thread for both.
